verdict.line: You lose if you walk up for CS into free Parrrley poke before level 6; you win once W (Path Maker) and Q's 2-stack pull are live and Remove Scurvy is down.

brief.thesis: Gangplank's Q (Parrrley) has 625 range, which outranges every K'Sante tool, so he pokes freely in the first few levels while you have no answer but to eat it or walk forward into it. The matchup flips once your Q (Ntofo Strikes) builds 2 stacks for its pull and W (Path Maker) comes off a shorter cooldown, because Gangplank's only counter to your stun is W (Remove Scurvy) on a 22-18s cooldown — once that's down he has nothing stopping the All Out (R) wall-knockback combo.

theirWindow.what: Don't commit your full stun combo — it gets cleansed for free. Poke back with Q or just wait it out before diving in.

yourWindow.what: Land 2 Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks for the pull, then follow with W (Path Maker)'s stun or R (All Out)'s wall knockback — he has no cleanse and no disengage besides Flash.

start.why: Grog-Soaked Blade's poison is magic damage ticking every auto trade — the magic resist on Helm (49.4% WR over 1657 games) blunts it directly, unlike Shield's flat HP.

boots.why: 84% pick rate and 47.3% WR; reduces the auto-attack damage GP stacks his poison on top of during extended poke exchanges.

core.why: Amplifies your Q (Ntofo Strikes) trade damage and gives the mana/CDR to spam Q stacks toward the 2-stack pull faster.
Omnivamp sustains you through poison ticks and lets you win extended trades even while behind on poke damage.
Stacking resists scale against his magic poison and any team-wide magic damage, completing the highest-WR path (52.5% over 141 games).

situational.when: the enemy team has stacked crit or on-hit damage you need to blunt in teamfights
gangplank or another enemy is stacking healing you need to shut off with grievous wounds
the enemy team is heavy magic damage and you need more sustain against burst

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained healing on trade procs offsets the chip damage from Parrrley and the Grog-Soaked Blade poison over a long poke-heavy laning phase.

summoners.why: 75% pick rate at 46.9% WR — Teleport lets you reset after buying Iceborn Gauntlet components and return to punish GP's lack of mobility once your all-in windows open.

playing.title: Farm safely under Q poke
playing.detail: His Q (Parrrley) outranges all of your abilities before level 6. Don't walk up for contested CS when it's up — let Second Wind and the poison's short duration handle the chip.

playing.title: Track Remove Scurvy cooldown
playing.detail: W (Remove Scurvy) clears any CC on him, including your W stun, on a 22-18s cooldown. Bait it out or wait for it before committing your full engage.

playing.title: Build Q stacks before engaging
playing.detail: Q (Ntofo Strikes) grants a stack on hit; at 2 stacks the next cast fires a shockwave that pulls him in. Land two Qs first so the pull itself closes the gap instead of relying on E.

playing.title: Punish all-ins after level 6
playing.detail: Once R (All Out) is up, knock him back through terrain and dash in behind — he has no reliable escape besides Flash, matching your measured solo-kill advantage.

playing.title: Use E to blunt a Parrrley
playing.detail: E (Footwork) is a dash plus shield on a 10-8s cooldown. Time it right as he fires Q to absorb the hit and immediately start closing distance.

playing.title: Rush Iceborn before forcing fights
playing.detail: Iceborn Gauntlet is your first core item in the highest-WR path (52.5%); its mana and CDR let you land Q stacks consistently enough to actually get the pull off.

playing.title: Use Teleport resets to punish immobility
playing.detail: After a back for Iceborn components, Teleport in behind his push — Gangplank has no gap-closer to retreat with once you're in range.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the ability readings, cooldown references, and tactical sequencing are this brief's own analysis.
